## Fully worked example

Download the [fully worked example](https://afsc-assessments.github.io/spmR/gt2026-handoff.zip) to get the
actual `ForProjections.dat`, `spm.dat` and `tacpar.dat` files, a plain-language
field guide, installation requirements, and a short R script for checking or
changing inputs, running a new attempt, plotting selected alternatives and
exporting useful CSV tables. The bundle includes one completed conditional
run and its provenance; new runs preserve it.

Open the [rendered Greenland turbot results](https://afsc-assessments.github.io/spmR/greenland_turbot.html) for
three Alternative 2 figures: spawning biomass and catch on logarithmic
y-axes, and fishing mortality on a linear y-axis. Dashed reference lines show
B40 and B35 on the spawning-biomass figure and F35 and F40 on the fishing-mortality
figure. Salmon ribbons show the 90% projection intervals. This example uses
Jim's confirmed local
47-value SSB history and diagnostic population-weight assumptions; successful
execution is separate from scientific input review. Figure downloads:
[spawning biomass](https://afsc-assessments.github.io/spmR/gt2026-figures/SSB.png),
[catch](https://afsc-assessments.github.io/spmR/gt2026-figures/Catch.png), and
[fishing mortality](https://afsc-assessments.github.io/spmR/gt2026-figures/F.png).

```{r}
#| include: false
if (file.exists(file.path("..", "DESCRIPTION"))) {
  pkgload::load_all("..", export_all = FALSE, helpers = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
} else {
  library(spmR)
}
example_candidates <- c(
  file.path("..", "examples", "gt_2026"),
  file.path("examples", "gt_2026")
)
example_dir <- example_candidates[
  file.exists(file.path(example_candidates, "run.R"))
][1]
if (is.na(example_dir)) {
  stop("Clone the spmR source repository to run this example.")
}
example_dir <- normalizePath(example_dir, mustWork = TRUE)
source(file.path(example_dir, "run.R"), local = TRUE)
raw_inputs <- gt2026_read_source(example_dir)
audit <- check_gt2026_inputs(example_dir)
history_counts_match <- length(raw_inputs$recruitment) == length(raw_inputs$ssb)
ssb_repeats_final_pair <- length(raw_inputs$ssb) >= 4L &&
  identical(tail(raw_inputs$ssb, 2L), head(tail(raw_inputs$ssb, 4L), 2L))
history_labels <- raw_inputs$lines[
  grepl("^# (Recruitment |SSB )", trimws(raw_inputs$lines))
]
```

The `examples/gt_2026` directory preserves the supplied Greenland turbot
projection files. The current species input contains
`r length(raw_inputs$recruitment)` recruitment values and
`r length(raw_inputs$ssb)` SSB values.
`r if (history_counts_match) "The counts match; their calendar alignment still requires confirmation." else "The counts differ, so the helper stops staging before creating an attempt directory."`
Population body weights, units, age and plus-group alignment, and SS3
export-field mapping also require confirmation before assessment use. This
article executes a read-only audit; it stages no files and generates no
projection results.

## Simple commands

Install the current spmR package and work from a clone of the
[source repository](https://github.com/afsc-assessments/spmR). From its root:

```{r}
#| eval: false
source("examples/gt_2026/run.R")
check_gt2026_inputs()
```

The audit reads the current source values. Confirm the recruitment and SSB
histories and their year alignment before staging. `diagnostic = TRUE` selects
working population weights, units and ages explicitly; it cannot supply
missing history values or establish their calendar alignment.
Once inputs are reviewed, each successful default staging call creates
`examples/gt_2026/spmR_runs/attempt-###`, retaining source snapshots, SHA-256
hashes, embedded declarations, and staging decisions. Existing attempt
directories are protected against overwriting.

## Audit the supplied files

The article locates and audits the example during its build. It requires the
source checkout or source package, where the example files are available.

```{r}
audit <- check_gt2026_inputs(example_dir)
gt::gt(audit)
```

The input recruitment basis is `r raw_inputs$recruitment_basis`. It contains
`r raw_inputs$recruitment_copies` recruitment copies with
`r length(raw_inputs$recruitment)` values each across
`r length(raw_inputs$recruitment_rows)` numeric lines, ending in
`r paste(tail(raw_inputs$recruitment, 2L), collapse = ", ")`.
The SSB series ends in
`r paste(tail(raw_inputs$ssb, 5L), collapse = ", ")`.
`r if (ssb_repeats_final_pair) "The final two SSB values repeat the preceding pair. Confirm that these are the intended source values rather than placeholders." else "Confirm these terminal SSB values against the source export."`

The source history labels are printed below. Counts alone establish neither
the calendar years nor the recruitment/SSB year pairing. Confirm both against
the SS3 export, including any labels that remain from an earlier revision.

```{r}
cat(history_labels, sep = "\n")
```

The helper accepts wrapped recruitment series and an explicit basis. With
matching source histories and declared inputs, it can stage one recruitment copy,
move the basis declaration into the versioned comment block, and replace four
zero spawning weights with `1e-12` for the positive-weight contract. It keeps
Tier 3 historical-recruitment mode (`Rec_Gen = 1`). That mode still requires
matching positional recruitment and SSB lengths.

The obsolete placeholder sidecar was removed from the canonical example;
earlier source snapshots remain archived. Separate JSON and native metadata
files are optional in version 0.4.3: the helper writes
validated declarations as comments in the staged species file. The current
native engine reads those comments directly. `spm.tpl` is self-contained and
requires no separate C++ header.

## Check staging readiness

The following table selects the current findings that need repair,
declarations, or review. It reads the audit without choosing diagnostic
assumptions or creating an attempt directory. The runner can repair duplicate
recruitment copies and zero spawning weights during staging; population
weights, units, and ages require explicit arguments or an explicit diagnostic
choice. Calendar alignment and the SS3 field definitions require scientific
review in either case.

```{r}
readiness <- audit[audit$status %in% c("missing", "review", "repair"), ]
readiness |>
  dplyr::rename(
    readiness_item = item,
    readiness_status = status,
    readiness_detail = detail
  ) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::cols_label(
    readiness_item = "item",
    readiness_status = "status",
    readiness_detail = "detail"
  )
```

## Stage complete inputs after review

Diagnostic mode uses `0.96 × fleet 1 + 0.04 × fleet 2` catch-weight proxies
separately for each sex as population weights. These coefficients are the
supplied fishing-mortality allocation. The mixture is a computational assumption
and requires review as a representation of population body weight. Diagnostic
mode also declares thousand fish, kg, tonnes, and ages 1–30 with a terminal
plus group. Whether the supplied spawning weights already incorporate maturity
requires confirmation; the all-one maturity fields are neutral multipliers. Under those fields,
`Ntot` and `SexRatio` describe all fish and the all-fish female fraction.

```{r}
#| eval: false
staged <- run_gt2026_projection(
  source_dir = example_dir,
  run_dir = tempfile("spmr-gt2026-article-"),
  diagnostic = TRUE,
  run = FALSE
)
staged$run_dir
```

This command is displayed without execution. It requires matching source
histories and an explicit decision to use the diagnostic assumptions.

## Run an explicitly chosen diagnostic projection

After confirming the histories and explicitly choosing the diagnostic assumptions, these commands enable native execution.
They are displayed without execution in this article.

```{r}
#| eval: false
gt2026 <- run_gt2026_projection(diagnostic = TRUE)
gt2026$summary
gt2026$run_dir
```

The helper uses `admb` on `PATH`, `SPMR_ADMB`, or its `admb` argument to compile
the installed template. `SPMR_CXX` selects a matching C++ compiler. A compatible
existing executable can be selected with `SPMR_EXECUTABLE` or `executable`.
If compilation still requests `spmr_input_v2.hpp`, reinstall spmR from the
current checkout and restart R to refresh the installed template.

A completed run under the supplied controls would contain 105,000 detail rows: seven alternatives, 1,000
simulations, and 15 projection years (2026–2040). The helper verifies the row
keys, finite outputs, initial biomass, fixed catches, and successful provenance.
Gradient and Hessian fit diagnostics are inapplicable to historical-recruitment
simulation. These checks establish the conditional calculation; the SS3 export
definitions and scientific interpretation require their own review.

## Replace the population-weight assumptions

Provide actual female and male population body-weight vectors with verified
units and age labels:

```{r}
#| eval: false
gt2026 <- run_gt2026_projection(
  population_weights = list(
    female = female_body_weights,
    male = male_body_weights
  ),
  units = verified_units,
  ages = verified_ages
)
```

Each vector must align with the 30 supplied age positions. Confirm the
beginning-of-2026 abundance state, plus group, and recruitment/SSB year pairing
against the SS3 export code and source fields. Supplying population weights
alone leaves those remaining checks open. The example README contains the
complete input evaluation and terminal commands.

## Standalone run-and-results report

`examples/gt_2026/greenland_turbot.qmd` provides visible manual run controls,
the current input audit, and three Alternative 2 figures. Spawning biomass
and catch use logarithmic y-axes; fishing mortality uses a linear y-axis.
Dashed reference lines show B40 and B35 on the spawning-biomass figure and
F35 and F40 on the fishing-mortality figure. All three figures show the
all-simulation median and a salmon 90% projection interval. Rendering performs
no projection; select a reviewed saved attempt
to populate the results. From the repository root:

```{bash}
#| eval: false
quarto render examples/gt_2026/greenland_turbot.qmd
quarto render examples/gt_2026/greenland_turbot.qmd -P saved_run:spmR_runs/attempt-001
```

The first command produces the audit only, including in a fresh source
checkout without saved output. The second selects results explicitly.

Replace `attempt-001` with the intended saved attempt. Saved results from an
older source revision are labelled separately from the current input audit.
